newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says it kills 18 Rwandan guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says it kills 18 Rwandan guerrillas.

text.p: Burundi's army said on Monday it intercepted and killed 18 Rwandan guerrillas attempting to return to Rwanda from Zaire through northwestern Burundi.
Army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi said 13 weapons were recovered on Sunday after the army intercepted the group of former Rwandan Hutu troops and Interahamwe militiamen.
"The criminals came from Zaire via the plain that faces Cibitoke (province). They wanted to penetrate Rwanda but our troops were on the lookout and stopped them from entering," he said.
There was no independent confirmation of the incident.
Cibitoke, the scene of some of the heaviest fighting in Burundi's civil war, divides eastern Zaire and southern Rwanda.
The province has been relatively quiet since Hutu rebels were driven from bases in eastern Zaire refugee camps last October, while the focus of fighting in Burundi has shifted to the south and east.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in civil war and massacres in Burundi since 1993, when the country's first freely elected Hutu president was murdered in an attempted coup.
An estimated 800,000 Rwandan Tutsis and Hutu moderates were slaughtered in Rwanda in 1994 in genocide by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs which fled Tutsi rebels who seized power the same year.
